oxidation-number.def: A bookkeeping charge given to each atom as if every bond were ionic, with shared electrons assigned to the more electronegative atom (also called oxidation state). A rise means electrons were lost; a fall means electrons were gained.

redox.def: A reaction in which electrons move from one species to another. Oxidation is loss of electrons (oxidation number rises); reduction is gain of electrons (oxidation number falls). The two always happen together.

half-reaction.def: An equation for just the oxidation or just the reduction part of a redox reaction, with the electrons shown, such as Zn → Zn²⁺ + 2e⁻.

oxidizing-agent.def: The oxidizing agent takes electrons from another species, so it is itself reduced; the reducing agent gives electrons to another species, so it is itself oxidized.
